claims.text: Elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding suffer significant Cr–Zr interdiffusion and associated premature failure during accident-relevant high-temperature exposure.
Alloying the Cr coating with approximately 2–5 wt% Si will inhibit elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Adding Si to the Cr coating will promote the formation of stable Cr silicide phases within the coating.
Cr silicide phases will act as diffusion barriers to zirconium transport into the chromium layer.
The proposed silicide diffusion barrier will reduce premature coating failure caused by Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Relative to elemental Cr, the Cr–Si coating will have a significantly thinner Cr–Zr interdiffusion layer during high-temperature steam exposure.
Relative to elemental Cr, the Cr–Si coating will retain better structural integrity during high-temperature steam exposure.
The Cr–Si coating will provide protective behavior under normal subcritical-water operation similar to that of elemental Cr.
Normal subcritical-water operation is represented by a temperature of approximately 300°C.
The beneficial effect of Si alloying will be most pronounced above approximately 800°C, including near 850°C.
The proposed benefit applies to short high-temperature transients with exposure times on the order of minutes.
A reduction greater than 50% in interdiffusion-layer thickness after steam exposure at approximately 850°C for 15 minutes is an example of the predicted discriminating improvement over elemental Cr.
